ai.definition: Advanced composites are engineered materials consisting of a matrix reinforced with fibres, designed to achieve superior mechanical properties such as high strength-to-weight ratios.
ai.howItWorks: Fibres embedded in a polymer or metal matrix provide the composite with enhanced stiffness and strength. The fibre orientation and matrix type can be tailored to meet specific performance requirements.
ai.problemSolved: Traditional materials often struggle to balance weight reduction, structural integrity, and cost-effectiveness. Advanced composites offer an optimized solution for these challenges, particularly in transportation sectors like automotive, aerospace, and marine industries.
ai.manufacturing: Manufacturing involves processes such as resin transfer moulding (RTM), vacuum infusion, and autoclave curing to bond the fibres with the matrix material. These processes require precision and controlled environments.
ai.buildProcess: The build process typically includes fibre preparation, matrix formulation, layup, curing, and post-processing steps. Each step must be carefully managed to ensure optimal composite performance.
ai.costDrivers: Cost drivers include raw material prices (fibres and matrices), manufacturing equipment costs, labor, and energy consumption during the production process.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook is positive due to increasing demand in high-performance applications. However, challenges remain in cost reduction and recycling.
ai.regulation: Regulations vary by industry but generally focus on safety standards, emissions, and end-of-life disposal. Certification processes are often required for aerospace and automotive applications.
ai.risks: Technical risks include material failure under extreme conditions, processing variability, and environmental impacts during manufacturing. Economic risks involve high initial costs and potential obsolescence due to rapid technological advancements.
ai.profitability: Profitability is variable depending on the specific application but can be substantial in sectors with high performance requirements such as aerospace and luxury vehicles.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development efforts will likely focus on reducing production costs, improving recycling processes, and expanding applications into new industries like renewable energy and construction.

glossary.def: The continuous phase of a composite material that surrounds and binds the fibres together.
Discrete reinforcing elements in a composite, typically made from materials like carbon or glass.
A process used to cure composites under high pressure and temperature conditions for optimal performance.

subsystems.name: Reinforcement fibres
subsystems.role: carry the load; the fibre choice sets most of the stiffness and strength.

subsystems.name: Matrix resin
subsystems.role: binds the fibres, spreads load between them and protects them.

subsystems.name: Fibre–matrix interface
subsystems.role: the bonding layer that decides whether a crack runs along fibres or is stopped.

subsystems.name: Layup and forming equipment
subsystems.role: places fibres in the designed directions.
parts: automatic tape and fibre placement machines

subsystems.name: Curing and consolidation
subsystems.role: solidifies the resin under heat and pressure.

subsystems.name: Machining, joining and inspection
subsystems.role: turns panels into structures and proves they have no hidden flaws.

buildSteps.title: Make the fibres
buildSteps.detail: Acrylic fibre is oxidised around 200–300 °C, then carbonised near 1,000–1,500 °C and sometimes graphitised hotter; glass is drawn as filaments from a melt.

buildSteps.title: Surface-treat and size
buildSteps.detail: Fibres are treated so resin grips them, then coated with a sizing that stops them fraying and handles cleanly.

buildSteps.title: Form the raw material
buildSteps.detail: Thousands of filaments are bundled into tows and either woven, or impregnated with partly cured resin to make prepreg tape.

buildSteps.title: Design the laminate
buildSteps.detail: Engineers choose a ply stack — fibre direction and count in each layer — so the part is stiff exactly where the loads run.

buildSteps.title: Lay up and shape
buildSteps.detail: Tape is laid by machine or by hand onto a mould on a tool shaped like the finished part.

buildSteps.title: Cure under heat and pressure
buildSteps.detail: Typically 120–180 °C with several bar of pressure in an autoclave, or under vacuum in a mould, until the resin cross-links and the plies consolidate.

buildSteps.title: Trim and machine
buildSteps.detail: Edges are cut to final shape; holes are drilled with diamond tools and sealed to prevent delamination.

buildSteps.title: Assemble
buildSteps.detail: Parts are bonded with structural adhesive, riveted or bolted, often to a metal frame, using the same fasteners as metal airframes.

buildSteps.title: Inspect
buildSteps.detail: Ultrasonic scanning looks for voids, delamination and resin-starved areas before the part flies.

prerequisites.why: carbon fibre begins as a textile fibre; capacity and energy cost set the price.
plain brittle resin cracks easily; modern formulas resist impact damage.
hand layup is too slow and inconsistent for large aircraft structures.
thermoset parts are hard to break down, so many end up as filler or cement feedstock.
aircraft and cars cannot be built on a material whose behaviour under fatigue is unproven.

pathway.milestone: half of the structural weight of widebody airliners is composite, alongside wind turbine blades and high-end road and race cars
pathway.unlocks: lighter vehicles and longer blades, with fewer joints and better corrosion resistance.

pathway.milestone: thermoplastic composites with cycle times measured in minutes
pathway.unlocks: mass-market car body panels and structural parts.

pathway.milestone: closed-loop recycling and bio-based resin feedstocks
pathway.unlocks: lower cost and a credible end-of-life story.

pathway.milestone: multifunctional laminates that also carry power, sense strain or store energy
pathway.unlocks: structures that integrate wiring and health monitoring rather than carrying it as extra weight.
